nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a timed function that maps each list $x$ of Booleans to an output list $f(x)$ of Booleans together with a declared time $t_f(x) \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $f$ computes in declared polynomial time when there is a polynomial $p$ with natural-number coefficients such that, for every list $x$ of Booleans, both $t_f(x)$ and the length of $f(x)$ are at most $p(|x|)$, where $|x|$ is the length of $x$.
nodes.title: Declared polynomial time for timed functions on bitstrings

nodes.summary: Let $L_1$ and $L_2$ be decision problems and let $f$ be a declared-time many-one reduction from $L_1$ to $L_2$. If the function sending $x$ to the output of $f$ on $x$ is polynomial-time computable by a Turing machine for the canonical bitstring encodings, then $L_1$ reduces to $L_2$ by a polynomial-time many-one reduction.
nodes.title: From declared-time to polynomial-time many-one reductions

nodes.summary: Let $L_1$ and $L_2$ be decision problems, let $f$ be a declared-time many-one reduction from $L_1$ to $L_2$, and let $g$ be a timed function from lists of Booleans to Booleans whose output on every list $y$ is $L_2(y)$. Then for every list $x$ of Booleans, the timed function that runs $f$ on $x$ and then $g$ on its output returns $L_1(x)$.
nodes.title: A declared-time reduction followed by a decider for the target decides the source

nodes.summary: Let $L_1$ and $L_2$ be decision problems, let $f$ be a declared-time many-one reduction from $L_1$ to $L_2$, and let $g$ be a timed function from lists of Booleans to Booleans that decides in declared polynomial time. Then the timed function that on input $x$ returns $g(f(x))$, with declared time the declared time of $f$ on $x$ plus that of $g$ on $f(x)$, decides in declared polynomial time.
nodes.title: Declared polynomial time is preserved under precomposition with a reduction

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a timed function that maps each list $x$ of Booleans to a Boolean $f(x)$ together with a declared time $t_f(x) \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $f$ decides in declared polynomial time when there is a polynomial $p$ with natural-number coefficients such that $t_f(x) \le p(|x|)$ for every list $x$ of Booleans, where $|x|$ is the length of $x$.
nodes.title: Declared polynomial time for timed deciders

nodes.summary: For every decision problem $L$, the timed identity function, which returns its input with declared time $0$, is a declared-time many-one reduction from $L$ to $L$.
nodes.title: Declared-time many-one reduction is reflexive

nodes.summary: Let $L_1$, $L_2$ and $L_3$ be decision problems. If $f_1$ is a declared-time many-one reduction from $L_1$ to $L_2$ and $f_2$ is a declared-time many-one reduction from $L_2$ to $L_3$, then the timed function that on input $x$ returns $f_2(f_1(x))$, with declared time the declared time of $f_1$ on $x$ plus that of $f_2$ on $f_1(x)$, is a declared-time many-one reduction from $L_1$ to $L_3$.
nodes.title: Declared-time many-one reductions compose

nodes.summary: Let $L_1$ and $L_2$ be decision problems and let $f$ be a timed function that maps each list $x$ of Booleans to a list $f(x)$ of Booleans together with a declared time. Then $f$ is a declared-time many-one reduction from $L_1$ to $L_2$ when $f$ computes in declared polynomial time and $L_1(x) = L_2(f(x))$ for every list $x$ of Booleans.
nodes.title: Declared-time many-one reduction by a timed function

nodes.summary: For every decision problem $L$ there is a timed function $f$ from lists of Booleans to Booleans that decides in declared polynomial time and whose output $f(x)$ equals $L(x)$ for every list $x$ of Booleans.
nodes.title: Every decision problem has a timed decider in declared polynomial time

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a decision problem, $p$ a polynomial with natural-number coefficients, and $V$ a timed function from pairs of lists of Booleans to Booleans that verifies $L$ with witness bound $p$. If the function sending $(x, w)$ to the output of $V$ on $(x, w)$ is polynomial-time computable by a Turing machine for the canonical bitstring encodings, then $L$ is in NP.
nodes.title: A timed verifier with polynomial-time output function puts its language in NP

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a decision problem and let $f$ assign to each bit string $x$ a timed computation, that is, a Boolean return value together with a declared time in $\mathbb{N}$, whose return value equals $L(x)$ for every $x$. If the function sending $x$ to the return value of $f(x)$ is polynomial-time computable, then $L$ belongs to the class P.
nodes.title: A timed decider with polynomial-time output function gives membership in P

nodes.summary: If a timed decider $f$ on bit strings has declared time bounded by a polynomial in the input length, then the verifier that sends an input $x$ and a witness $w$ to $f(x)$, ignoring $w$, has declared time bounded by a polynomial in $|x| + |w|$.
nodes.title: A decider with polynomial declared time gives a verifier with polynomial declared time

nodes.summary: A timed verifier $V$, which assigns to each pair of bit strings $(x, w)$ (an input and a witness) a timed computation returning a Boolean, runs in declared polynomial time when there is a polynomial $q$ with natural coefficients such that the declared time of $V(x, w)$ is at most $q(|x| + |w|)$ for all $x$ and $w$.
nodes.title: Verifiers with polynomial declared time

nodes.summary: Let $L_1$ and $L_2$ be decision problems, let $f$ be a declared polynomial-time many-one reduction from $L_1$ to $L_2$, and let $V$ be a verifier with polynomial declared time that verifies $L_2$ with witness bound $p$. Let $V'$ be the verifier that on input $x$ and witness $w$ first runs $f$ on $x$, obtaining $y$, then runs $V$ on $(y, w)$ and accepts when $V$ accepts and $|w| \le p(|y|)$; its declared time is the…
nodes.title: Pulling a verifier back along a declared reduction

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a decision problem and let $f$ be a timed decider whose return value on every bit string $x$ equals $L(x)$. Then the verifier that sends an input $x$ and a witness $w$ to $f(x)$, ignoring $w$, verifies $L$ with the zero polynomial as witness bound, so only the empty witness is allowed.
nodes.title: A decider is a verifier with witness bound zero

nodes.summary: A timed verifier $V$, which assigns to each pair of bit strings $(x, w)$ (an input and a witness) a timed computation returning a Boolean, verifies a decision problem $L$ with witness bound $p$, a polynomial with natural coefficients, when for every bit string $x$, $L(x)$ holds if and only if there is a witness $w$ with $|w| \le p(|x|)$ such that $V(x, w)$ returns true.
nodes.title: Verifying a decision problem with a witness bound

inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.
